messages:
zoe wu: quick sync: onboarding mag-13b-int4v3 showed reproducible 'phase alias' after very long priming (~9k tokens). not normal.

zoe wu: symptom: token insertion/shift happens at deterministic offsets, e.g. words repeating one token earlier. low-level dump points to RoPE remap producing different angle bins between fp16 and int4v3.

ravi kumar: can you share the small repro? is this specific to our new spectral downsample stage in the compiler?

zoe wu: yes, repro attached in ticket. run:```bash
python tests/repro_long_priming.py --model mag-13b-int4v3 --prompt long_news_convo.txt 
```
repro is ~90% stable on my workstation.

mike t: logs show a repeating pattern every ~192 tokens in the kv position diffs. that spacing screams tiling boundary. i think the spectral downsampler reduces phase fidelity for positions that fall into the same spectral bucket.

zoe wu: i hashed per-pos KV keys and diffed fp16 vs int4v3. diffs start at pos ~8736 and then at 8928/9120 etc (stride 192). attaching small CSV.

ci-bot: CI: triggered nightly/quant-long-priming (mag-13b-int4v3) (job id 2026-03-21_0750) :robot_face:

ravi kumar: hypothesis: when compiler packs rotary embeddings into spectral bands we quantize the band coefficients with a per-band scale. the band width currently equals block_size=192 in codegen. cumulative rounding inside band could skew phase for high positions.

mike t: quick experiment: rebuilt compiler with band_size=96 and ran same prompt. drift point moved later (~9800) and cluster spacing halved to 96. so it's correlated.

zoe wu: interesting. so reducing band_size reduces aliasing but increases compute because of more bands. any non-invasive patch ideas?

ravi kumar: two options: 1) apply spectral-preserve interpolation that stores extra high-freq residuals per band (small memory increase), 2) pad band vectors to avoid fractional tail when int4 lanes pack (similar to tile padding).

ops-jen: heads up: if you change band_size or add padding that raises per-token memory bandwidth, Dedicated mag64 nodes might hit autoscale thresholds. suggest a canary with 2% traffic first.

mike t: i ran a quick microbench: padding bands to 256 (zero-fill tails) removed the aliasing completely in my run and only increased token latency by ~2ms on mag64. throughput drop negligible at low concurrency.

zoe wu: good. can we try a hybrid patch that pads only bands that would have fractional packing (i.e., when vector_len % pack_width != 0)? smaller overhead.

ravi kumar: yes i'll code that. also adding a unit test that fuzzes band sizes and validates per-pos phase closeness to fp16 across 12 random seeds.

ci-bot: artifact uploaded: s3://redwood-ci/quant-longpriming/1765559999/artifacts.tgz

mike t: small note: the regression only shows up on long priming (>8k) and with certain prompts (dense noun-phrase repetition). short prompts unaffected. so fallback routing for long priming is reasonable short-term.

zoe wu: creating INC-2026-0750 to track. temporary routing: if priming_len > 8000 && model_tag includes 'int4v3' -> fallback fp16. ops advised.

ops-jen: routing rule applied. also flagged Dedicated upgrades to avoid kernel changes until we validate patch.

ravi kumar: PR opened: github.com/redwood/infer/pull/8492 (patch: pad spectral bands only when pack tail non-zero + unit tests).

mike t: ran nfuzz with band_padding enabled across tiles 64/96/128/192. no reproductions over 1000 fuzz runs.

zoe wu: excellent. i'll run full canary (2% traffic) after CI passes and share token-match/perp table for priming lengths [4k,8k,12k].

ravi kumar: if canary looks clean we can gradually remove fallback. target: keep int4v3 for general traffic but route long priming heavy customers to fp16 until two-week stable window.

ci-bot: CI pass (quant-longpriming): all tests green. artifact link above.

zoe wu: thanks all. follow-up: we should add a small eval into the onboard checklist: run longpriming sweep to 12k with kv-hash diffs and a band-tiling sanity check. will draft checklist entry.

mike t: note for docs: add explanation of spectral band sizing tradeoff to onboarder guide so new compilers avoid surprises.

zoe wu: closing loop here after canary. will update ticket INC-2026-0750 with results.
